question:
A 33-year-old male presents with anxiety and ongoing moodiness, citing stress at home and work. His
medical history includes chronic gastritis previously treated for *Helicobacter pylori*, chronic
pyelonephritis with kidney stones, and stage 1 chronic kidney disease. He also has an 8-year smoking
history and has unsuccessfully attempted to quit using nicotine patches, experiencing recurrent anxiety
during those attempts. His grandfather, a heavy smoker, recently passed away from metastatic lung
cancer. The patient’s vital signs and physical examination are normal. His provider is considering
prescribing a partial nicotine agonist. Which test should be performed prior to initiating this therapy?
Answer Choices: (A) Electrocardiogram (B) Mini-Mental State Examination (C) Pulmonary function
testing (D) Complete blood count (E) Serum potassium levels (F) 9-item patient health questionnaire
(G) Echocardiography (H) Liver function tests (I) Creatinine (J) Fagerström Test for Nicotine
Dependence
 A. Mini-Mental State Examination
B. Electrocardiogram
C. 9-item patient health questionnaire
D. Echocardiography
E. Liver function tests
F. Pulmonary function testing
G. Complete blood count
H. Serum potassium levels

I. Creatinine
J. Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence
